meta.note: The City of Austin — the state capital and Travis County’s seat — is a separate government from the county, run council-manager style: an elected Mayor (Kirk Watson) and 10 district council members set policy, and a City Manager (T.C. Broadnax) runs operations. The bars are the General Fund’s departmental operating budget ($1.49B); Police, Fire, and EMS together are more than 60% of it. Austin’s full budget across every fund is about $6.3 billion — most of the difference is self-supporting utilities like Austin Energy ($1.38B) and Austin Water ($864M). One note on arithmetic: the departments below foot to the $1.49B operating total; the ~$54M gap to the often-quoted $1.54B General Fund is transfers-out and reserves booked fund-wide. Every dollar traces to the city’s open-data budget portal.
facts: Police, Fire, and EMS together are more than 60% of the General Fund’s operating budget.
Austin owns its electric utility — Austin Energy — a $1.38 billion enterprise fund.
After voters rejected Proposition Q in November 2025, the council cut the tax rate to $0.524017 per $100 (from an adopted $0.574017).
This is the CITY of Austin; Travis County ($2.16B all funds) is a separate government.
